newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn leader condemns violence in church arson.
newsitem.headline: Bonn leader condemns violence in church arson.

text.p: The president of Germany's parliament called on Germans to condemn all forms of violence after inspecting the burned ruins of a Luebeck church destroyed in an arson attack by right-wing extremists.

Rita Suessmuth, president of the lower house of parliament, said the attack on the St. Vicelin church on Sunday was a reprehensible crime and said it was not enough to clamp down on extremists with laws alone.
"Violence cannot be stopped only with the help of legislation," Suessmuth said. "All citizens have to work together to realise the goal of stopping all forms of violence."

Suspected neo-Nazis daubed swastikas on the facade of St Vicelin Church and set a fire which spread to the church. They also scrawled the name of a local priest whose parish is sheltering a family of asylum seekers to prevent their deportation back to Algeria.
The northern state of Schleswig-Holstein said it was offering a reward of 50,000 marks for information on the fire.
"Such perpetrators must not be able to hide behind a curtain of silence and find silent acceptance," state interior minister Ekkehard Wienholtz told Berlin radio.

The attack, which gutted the Roman Catholic church, sparked memories of a wave of racist violence after German unification in 1990 in which asylum-seekers' hostels became frequent targets of firebomb attacks.

Luebeck Mayor Michael Bouteiller has said the city's efforts to protect the rights of foreigners were a "provocation" to extreme right-wingers and appealed to the authorities to put an end to the violence by banning all extreme rightist parties.
Police commissioned an unusually large team of 40 detectives on the case. They suspect extreme right-wingers and prosecutors are treating the attack as aggravated arson.

Protestant priest Guenther Harig, whose name was scrawled on the St Vicelin church but who works in another parish, gave refuge to a family of Algerian asylum-seekers inside his church after authorities refused them asylum at the beginning of May.
